_comment: Frozen RFC-0007 §10 port debt. The gate fails if any count RISES; lower it by fixing violations, then re-run --write-baseline. Every entry must carry a reason and a phase in the migration playbook.

SP-0005.due: before any service enters Phase 2 of the migration playbook
SP-0005.why_frozen_and_not_fixed_here: These live in three service repositories, not in ci-workflows, so this repository cannot fix them. They are frozen so the lane can be introduced green and so a SEVENTH cannot be added while they are outstanding.
findings: inboxxhq-configuration-service: contract declares http=4031, grpc=50091, metrics=9132 - ledger-service's entire port triple, copied. Infra publishes 4033/50093/9135.
inboxxhq-order-service: contract declares http=4102, metrics=9152 - allocated to no service at all. Infra publishes 4030/9131.
inboxxhq-voice-ai-agent-service: contract declares websocket=4023 - realtime-gateway's HTTP port. Either a fourth listener needing an RFC-0007 §4.1 amendment, or dead.
SP-0005.note: Nothing dials service.contract.yaml, which is why none of these has caused an outage and why all six could accumulate unseen. They block the migration rather than production: the migration's safety rests on checking a service's ports against a source of truth, and these are the file a reviewer consults to do that.

SP-0007.due: per service, before that service enters Phase 2
SP-0007.why_frozen_and_not_fixed_here: SP-0007 is an ADVISORY cross-check and is never the gate for this number. The authoritative ratchet is inboxxhq-infra scripts/check-service-addressing.py, which froze the same 321 and is already shrinking it; ARCH-0010 in inboxxhq-architecture-check gates the application-code half at Error severity. The number is recorded here only so a reader of the port controls sees it, and it is expected to track the infra ratchet exactly. If the two ever disagree, one of the three patterns has drifted and that is itself the finding.
